name: A Tribe Called Quest
editorial_article:
A Tribe Called Quest was an influential American hip-hop group formed in Queens, New York City, in 1985. Comprising Q-Tip, Phife Dawg, Ali Shaheed Muhammad, and Jarobi White, the group became central figures in the Native Tongues collective. They are widely recognized as pioneers of alternative hip-hop and jazz rap, blending sophisticated, jazz-infused production with intelligent, rhythmic lyricism. Critics have frequently cited them as one of the most artistic and significant acts in the history of hip-hop, with their 1990 debut, People's Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm, earning the first five-mic rating in The Source magazine.

The group's evolution throughout the 1990s helped define the sound of East Coast hip-hop. Albums like The Low End Theory and Midnight Marauders are considered landmark releases that bridged the gap between jazz and rap, achieving platinum status and critical acclaim. After a period of inactivity, the group reunited for their final studio album, We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service, released in 2016. Featuring posthumous contributions from Phife Dawg, the project served as a poignant conclusion to their storied career.
